I'll pull your intents and run LedgerMind's analysis.
# Short answer: the spending itself is fine — the *authorizations* are the problem

**Actual spend: $1.28 across 4 payments. Authorized: $67.** All 4 payments have receipts, none breached a cap, and every payment went to an allowlisted merchant where a list existed. Your agent is behaving. Your guardrails are loose.

Risk level: **medium**. Four things, in priority order:

### 🔴 Fix now

**1. Unrestricted merchant list on your ops intent** — `0x568222...2f5b`
$10 total cap, $2/tx, **empty allowlist** (agent can pay anyone), and **zero payments in 30 days**. Unused *and* unbounded is the worst pairing: no upside, full blast radius. Either pin it to specific merchants, or if you can't name who it's supposed to pay, it has no defined job — revoke it.

**2. $0.80 stranded on a revoked intent** — `0xe88b02...df16`
The Q3 marketing trial was revoked ("tool not adopted") with $1.00 funded and only $0.20 spent. That $0.80 can never be spent — it's 100% of your idle capital. `withdrawRemainder` gets it back, no downside.

### 🟡 This week

**3. Cloud infra agent looks like it's hitting a ceiling, not paying an invoice** — `0x4e0866...bcf4`
Both payments were **$0.49 against a $0.50 per-tx cap — 98%, twice, same merchant, 7 seconds apart.** That pattern suggests the cap is setting the amount rather than the bill. Also: it burned 49% of its $2 total cap in a single day while labeled "weekly" autopay — at that rate the cap binds before the window closes.

⚠️ **Caveat worth taking seriously:** there's no invoice data, so I can't confirm whether those payments were clipped to fit the cap or genuinely cost $0.49. Check one real infra invoice before raising anything. If the true bill is $0.49, this is a non-issue.

**4. Research intent over-authorized ~500x** — `0xb530e9...7ca7`
$50 cap (75% of your total authorization) against $0.10 of spend. The single-merchant allowlist contains the risk, so this is lower priority — but the headroom bears no relation to demonstrated need.

### What I couldn't verify

All 4 payments landed on a **single day** (2026-09-13) despite the 30-day window, so I can't confirm burn rate, trend, or the "weekly" cadence. The throttling read above rests entirely on two transactions seconds apart — treat it as a flag to investigate, not a conclusion. Merchant addresses also have no names; I'm inferring `0x1111` is your infra vendor from the intent description, not from data.

**Bottom line:** nothing here indicates agent misbehavior. Do the two "now" items (~5 minutes, recovers $1.10 and closes your only uncontained exposure), then check an infra invoice before touching caps.

data.headline: Spend is tiny and fully receipted, but three control problems stand out: 0.80 USDC stranded on a revoked intent, an unrestricted-merchant Active intent authorised for 10 USDC with zero usage, and the cloud-infra agent hitting 98% of its per-tx cap on both payments.

findings.title: Cloud infra agent is being throttled by its per-tx cap
findings.detail: Both payments on 0x4e0866d3c7ac1acbd4058cc9a0877193e640bcf4 were 0.49 USDC against a 0.50 perTxCap — 98% utilisation twice in a row, to the same merchant, seconds apart. That pattern is consistent with the agent splitting or truncating a payment to fit the ceiling rather than paying the true invoice amount. The intent has also burned 49% of its 2 USDC total cap in a single day while described as a weekly autopay, so the total cap is likely to bind before the 30-day window closes.

findings.title: Idle capital on a revoked intent
findings.detail: 0xe88b02abd36a10617386cd71105ff39276ccdf16 was revoked after the marketing tool trial ended, but 0.80 of the 1.00 USDC funded remains on-contract. It is unrecoverable by spending (the intent is Revoked) and only withdrawRemainder frees it. This is 100% of the reported idle capital in the account.

findings.title: Unrestricted merchant allowlist on an unused discretionary intent
findings.detail: 0x568222982112b7bd55bd90524e1434472f422f5b is Active with a 10 USDC total cap, 2 USDC per tx, an empty allowlist (unrestrictedMerchants = true), and zero payments in 30 days. An open allowlist on the second-largest cap in the account means any counterparty the agent picks can be paid, and there is no observed behaviour to justify the authorisation. Unused plus unbounded is the worst combination: no benefit, full blast radius.

findings.title: Research intent is over-authorised by roughly 500x observed spend
findings.detail: 0xb530e9ca418560028db414e09aa36617a89e7ca7 carries the largest cap in the account (50 USDC, 75% of the 67 USDC total authorisation) against 0.10 USDC of actual spend in a single payment at 2% of its per-tx cap. The allowlist is restricted to one merchant, which contains the risk, but the authorisation headroom bears no relation to demonstrated need.

findings.title: Payment hygiene is clean
findings.detail: All 4 payments carry receipts, each landed with an allowlisted merchant where a list exists, and merchant concentration is explainable (0x1111 is the infra vendor). No payment exceeded its per-tx cap and no intent exceeded its total cap. The problems here are authorisation sizing, not agent misbehaviour.

actions.rationale: A 10 USDC Active intent with an empty allowlist and zero payments is the largest uncontained exposure in the account. Pin it to the specific merchants the ops agent is actually meant to pay; if none can be named, this intent has no defined job and should be revoked instead.

Intent is already Revoked with the trial abandoned; the 0.80 USDC funded balance can never be spent and is the entirety of idle capital reported. withdrawRemainder returns it immediately with no downside.

Two consecutive payments at 98% of the 0.50 per-tx cap indicate the cap, not the invoice, is setting the amount. Raise it to clear the true infra invoice in one transaction so payments stop being clipped or split — but confirm the real invoice size first, and pair the change with a total-cap review since 49% of the 2 USDC cap went in one day on a stated weekly schedule.

50 USDC of authorisation supports 0.10 USDC of spend and represents 75% of total account authorisation. Cutting the cap toward observed subscription cost shrinks the blast radius with no operational impact; the single-merchant allowlist means this is lower priority than the unrestricted intent above.

dataGaps: All 4 payments and all dailySpend rows fall on a single day (2026-09-13) despite a 30-day window, so trend, burn rate and the 'weekly' cadence claimed by 0x4e0866...bcf4 cannot be verified — the throttling read rests on two transactions 7 seconds apart.
No invoice or expected-amount data, so it cannot be confirmed whether the 0.49 USDC payments were truncated to fit the 0.50 cap or genuinely cost 0.49.
Merchant addresses have no names or categories; concentration on 0x1111...1111 is assumed to be the infra vendor from the intent purpose, not from the data.
No funding history or timestamps, so it is unclear whether the thin funding levels (0.3, 0.4, 1.2 USDC) reflect deliberate drip-funding or pending top-ups against the much larger caps.
idleDays is 0 on every intent including the Revoked one, which is inconsistent with it holding an unspent balance; the idle-age signal cannot be trusted.
